message.content:
In Blackjack an Ace is a “flexible” card – it can count as either **1** or **11**, whichever is more advantageous to the hand without causing a bust.  

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Two Aces** | One Ace counts as 11, the other as 1 (so the hand totals 12). |
| **Ace + 10‑value card** | This is a “natural” Blackjack (21). |
| **Ace + 9** | You may choose 20 (11+9) or 10 (1+9), but most players will take 20. |
| **Ace + 8** | You can play it as 19 (11+8) or 9 (1+8). |
| **Ace + 7** | You can play it as 18 (11+7) or 8 (1+7). |
| **Ace + 6** | You can play it as 17 (11+6) or 7 (1+6). |
| **Ace + 5** | You can play it as 16 (11+5) or 6 (1+5). |
| **Ace + 4** | You can play it as 15 (11+4) or 5 (1+4). |
| **Ace + 3** | You can play it as 14 (11+3) or 4 (1+3). |
| **Ace + 2** | You can play it as 13 (11+2) or 3 (1+2). |
| **Ace + 1 (another Ace)** | Same as two Aces: 12. |

If at any point the hand’s total exceeds 21, the Ace automatically “drops” from 11 to 1 to avoid busting. This flexibility is what makes the Ace such a powerful card in Blackjack.
